era: PlayStation 2 / Xbox / PSP / HD consoles / PC / Switch
summary: Criterion and EA's high-speed crash-racing series, covering the original trilogy, Revenge, handheld entries, Paradise, Crash, and Paradise Remastered.

emulation.notes: Use original Xbox hardware or check Xbox emulator compatibility.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Xbox output or Xbox emulation

primary.why: The first Burnout launched on PS2 and later reached GameCube and Xbox. With no platform-exclusive content documented, the Xbox version is the strongest hardware/fidelity route among the original releases.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox version on original hardware or a compatible Xbox emulator; use PS2/GameCube only if those are the available copies.

emulation.notes: Use original Xbox hardware or check Xbox emulator compatibility.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Xbox output or Xbox emulation

primary.why: The Xbox Developer's Cut adds 21 car skins, 15 additional Crash mode tracks for 30 total, Xbox Live leaderboards, and custom soundtrack support. It is the most complete release.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox Developer's Cut on original Xbox hardware or a compatible Xbox emulator.

emulation.emulator: Original Xbox / Xbox 360 Xbox Originals / xemu if compatible
emulation.notes: Use official Xbox hardware routes where possible; online modes are no longer available.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Xbox output or Xbox emulation

primary.version: Xbox release via Xbox Originals where owned
primary.why: Burnout 3 released on PS2 and Xbox, with the Xbox release later reissued on Xbox 360 through Xbox Originals. The Xbox route has the strongest hardware/fidelity ceiling and preserves the online/local feature set as much as current service availability allows.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox version on original Xbox or an Xbox 360 with the Xbox Originals release if already owned; online services for the original game were shut down in 2010.

emulation.emulator: Xbox backward compatibility / Xenia if compatible
emulation.notes: Prefer official Xbox backward compatibility; online features are no longer available.

primary.why: The Xbox 360 version adds improved graphics, ten new Crash junctions, improved online systems, Burnout Clips, marketplace cars, and later Xbox One/Series backward compatibility. It is the most complete and best-preserved version, even though online servers are shut down.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox 360 version on Xbox 360 or backward-compatible Xbox One/Series hardware; treat online features as historical only.

emulation.notes: Use PPSSPP for higher-resolution PSP play.

primary.why: Burnout Legends repackages tracks and modes from the first three Burnout games for handheld play. The PSP version received much stronger critical reception and includes PSP-exclusive collector car Wi-Fi mechanics, while the DS port was poorly received.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PSP version on original hardware or PPSSPP with internal-resolution upscale.

entries.title: Burnout Dominator
entries.definitive_edition: PS2 version plus PSP DLC track supplement

emulation.notes: Use PCSX2 for main play and PPSSPP only for preserved PSP DLC tracks.

primary.why: Dominator released on PS2 and PSP. The PS2 version is the higher-fidelity main route, while the PSP version received two downloadable tracks, Carnival City and Red Gate, making it a secondary content supplement.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 version on original hardware or PCSX2; use the PSP version only for its downloadable track content if preserved.

secondary.exclusive_content: Carnival City and Red Gate downloadable tracks
secondary.what_to_play: Play the PSP version's DLC tracks if you can access a preserved legitimate copy.
secondary.why: The PSP route is lower fidelity but has source-documented extra tracks.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster exists; Crash Mode is absent by design.

entries.title: Burnout Paradise
entries.definitive_edition: Original PS3/Xbox 360 with all DLC installed; otherwise use Burnout Paradise Remastered

emulation.emulator: Original console / RPCS3 / Xenia if compatible
emulation.notes: Use original console entitlements for DLC completeness; prefer Remastered for current PC play.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original HD console output, potentially higher via emulator

primary.version: Original version with console DLC installed
primary.why: The original Paradise released on PS3, Xbox 360, and Windows. The Windows Ultimate Box has enhanced PC display options but did not include every later console DLC pack at launch; Big Surf Island and Cops and Robbers were console DLC. For the original 2008 release family, PS3/Xbox 360 with all DLC installed is the most complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play an original PS3 or Xbox 360 copy with the full DLC set already purchased/installed; otherwise use Paradise Remastered on PC for the modern complete route.

entries.remaster_caveats: Original online services shut down in August 2019; Remastered is tracked separately and is the modern complete route.

emulation.notes: Because it is a downloadable title, entitlement availability is the key preservation issue.

primary.why: Burnout Crash! released on PS3, Xbox 360, and iOS. The Xbox 360 version includes Kinect mode, making it the most complete feature route, though it remains a downloadable/spin-off crash-game entry.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox 360 XBLA version if already owned; use Kinect only if you specifically want its exclusive control mode.

entries.title: Burnout Paradise Remastered

emulation.notes: Native Windows remaster. No emulator needed; capture directly from PC and verify EA app/Steam sign-in before recording.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Native PC remaster at 4K/60 capture settings

primary.why: The remaster is the complete modern package and the Windows release has the highest practical capture ceiling: high-resolution output, 60 fps target, controller support, and no console capture constraints. The remaster includes the Year of Paradise add-ons, including Big Surf Island; the Switch version has the same 8 main DLC packs, so there is no content reason to choose a console route.
primary.how_to_play: Use the current Windows release through EA app or Steam, install/verify the latest patch, and capture at 4K/60 with a stable controller profile. Treat online Freeburn as optional because EA online services can change; the archive-critical content is the remastered base game plus DLC island, bikes, cars, party, boost, Cagney, and Cops and Robbers content.

entries.remaster_caveats: This entry is for the 2018 remaster, not the 2008 original or The Ultimate Box. The remaster includes the major Year of Paradise add-ons, including Big Surf Island, Cops and Robbers, bikes, vehicles, party, boost, and Cagney content; online service availability should be checked before any multiplayer-focused episode.
